analysis.title: Global Server: Raising both AI and General servers; better mix and higher memory costs drive CSP spending
key_insights: GS raises its global server value TAM by 31% / 45% in 2027 / 28E, driven by higher forecasts for both general servers and AI servers. Global server revenue is forecast at US$604,976m in 2026E, US$1,114,623m in 2027E and US$1,602,489m in 2028E.

General servers: value raised 17% / 11% in 2027 / 28E, with both shipments and ASP raised. Shipments are forecast to grow 20% / 12% / 8% YoY in 2026-28E, and general server revenue is raised 15% / 13% / 11% in 2026-28E on high memory costs and specification upgrades tied to AI workloads.
General server value TAM is forecast to grow at a 22% CAGR in 2025-28E to US$271bn, or 17% of global server value TAM by 2028E, down from 46% in 2025.

AI server racks (NVL72, NVIDIA and AMD): shipments raised 5% / 1% to 110k / 164k racks in 2027 / 28E. Rack shipments are forecast to grow 238% / 75% / 49% YoY in 2026-28E. The rack value TAM is forecast to grow at a 163% CAGR in 2025-28E to US$1tn, or 63% of global server value TAM by 2028E.

NVIDIA-powered racks are forecast at 61k / 97k / 149k in 2026-28E versus 50k / 92k / 148k previously. The increase reflects higher forecasts for brand makers (Dell, SuperMicro, HP), higher US CSP capex, and NVIDIA chipset shipments raised 9% / 15% in 2027 / 28E.

AI servers (8-GPU, GPU and ASIC): shipments raised 10% / 29% to 2.7m / 3.3m in 2027 / 28E, mainly on rising ASIC-based server demand. 2026E shipments are cut 7% to 1.7m as US CSPs shift toward higher-density racks. 8-GPU value TAM is forecast to grow at a 38% CAGR in 2025-28E to US$318bn, or 20% of the total by 2028E.

The new shipment forecasts imply AI chip demand of 18m / 29m / 38m in 2026-28E (+84% / +59% / +31% YoY). Implied ASIC penetration is about 60% globally and about 50% among global-tier hyperscalers in 2028E, and 92% among Chinese buyers.

US CSP capex is forecast to grow 84% / 52% / 13% YoY in 2026-28E, with estimates raised 4% / 17% / 22%, reaching US$1,397bn by 2028E. China CSP capex is forecast to grow 105% / 21% / 14% YoY, with estimates raised 14% / 15% / 11%.

Capex mix: chipsets (GPU, ASIC, CPU) remain the largest contributor, followed by memory (HBM), then networking and other components such as cooling, power, chassis and rail kits. China CSP chip spending is expected to be more diversified across GPUs and ASICs than at global CSPs.

Microsoft's Maia 300 announcement: Azure Maia expands to multi-gigawatt deployments as the primary inference system for Microsoft products. Multi-gigawatt deployment begins in 2027, and reports point to a possible plan for more than 1M Maia 300 chips in 2027.

CPU launches support general server demand from agentic AI: Intel Xeon 6+ (Computex 2026), Intel Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids (shown Aug 2026), and AMD 6th Gen EPYC Venice, in production ramp since May. GS frames CPU servers as the control plane for agentic AI workloads.
Among ODMs, GS expects Hon Hai / FII to keep the leading position and gain share on continued specification upgrades. Hon Hai ODM-direct rack shipments are forecast at 25k / 59k / 101k in 2026-28E.
Historical trend: in 1Q26 global brand server value was +103% YoY and ODM direct +2% YoY. Non-x86 servers were 50% of global server value TAM in 1Q26, while x86 servers were -5% YoY.

Supply chain Buy list: Hon Hai / FII, Wiwynn, Wistron, Innolight, Eoptolink, Shengyi Tech, Victory Giant, FOCI, Largan, LandMark, VPEC, AVC, Fositek, Auras, King Slide, EMC, GCE, TSMC, MPI, WinWay, Aspeed and Hon Precision. Exhibit 4 gives 2026E revenue exposure of each name to chip platforms such as NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Amazon Trainium and Chinese GPUs / ASICs.

PCs: shipments are forecast at -14% / -5% / 0% YoY in 2026E-28E, with global PC ASP +10% in 2026E. Smartphones: shipments are forecast at -10% / +2% / +2% YoY in 2026-28E, and foldable shipments rise to 35.0m in 2026E and 66.1m in 2027E.

sector_views.rationale: AI server value TAM is forecast to grow 119% / 123% / 54% YoY in 2026-28E, with rack-level servers reaching 63% of global server value by 2028E.
Value forecasts are raised on higher shipments and ASP, driven by memory costs and CPU specification upgrades for agentic AI workloads.
Shipments are forecast to fall 14% in 2026E and 5% in 2027E before flattening in 2028E.
Shipments are forecast to fall 10% in 2026E, then grow 2% in each of 2027E and 2028E.

risk_factors: A shift toward higher-density AI racks at leading US CSPs cuts 8-GPU AI server shipments in 2026E by 7% to 1.7m.
AI server growth depends on CSP capex, which GS forecasts to slow from 84% growth in 2026E to 13% in 2028E for US CSPs.

Exhibit 1 labels global server value TAM revisions of +0% / +31% / +45% for 2026-28E, with AI servers +119% / +123% / +54% YoY and general servers +47% / +15% / +8% YoY in 2026-28E.
Exhibit 9 labels 2025-28E CAGRs of 22% for general servers, 163% for AI server racks (NVL72) and 38% for AI servers (8-GPU).

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising CSP capex, fabless shipments and foundry capacity drive higher AI server and AI chip demand through 2028E.
ASIC-based servers are optimized for AI computation with better efficiency, and new ASIC generations from leading CSPs support AI server growth.
